question.text: An Automatic Conversion Clause in a hybrid security:

answer.text: Gives the investor an option to convert at any time of their choosing
Automatically converts equity back into debt if the company misses targets
Mandates compulsory conversion of convertible debt or preference shares into equity on occurrence of a pre-defined trigger (e.g., IPO, revenue milestone)
Requires 75% shareholder approval for every conversion event

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.6.8 (Automatic Conversion Clause), convertible debt or preference shares MUST compulsorily convert to equity on occurrence of a pre-defined trigger — e.g., startup reaching INR 10 crore revenue, Pre-Series A capital raise, or IPO. Optional conversion is the opposite concept. The Trap: Option A describes optional conversion. Option C inverts the mechanism. Option D invents a shareholder-approval gate. Cross-Exam Context: Conversion triggers tested in XIX-A (product) and VIII (Equity Derivatives) for embedded-option valuation. Manager's Pro-Tip: When drafting the trigger, be surgical: 'IPO on recognized stock exchange with minimum issue size INR X and minimum price Y'. Vague triggers ('successful IPO') invite litigation when the company tries to argue the trigger didn't crystallize.
